116.t: Green sheet school gigs and giving up electric keyboards

116.t: The Fender Rhodes and why electric piano ends jazz clubs
116.s: He argues the electric piano detaches the music from its tradition, with a NOCCA ear-test.
116.q: six months, and it died. I wasn’t even sorry. But one of the things that I did realize – first of all, in my case, I was not a club owner. That’s the first thing. 78.t: Playing a grand piano for a night at the American Legion
78.s: He plays only organ now, but played a grand piano at an upstairs Legion party and enjoyed the two-beat sound with his drummer.
78.ch: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
78.q: : Strictly I play the organ, with the exception of last Saturday night. They had a birthday upstairs in the American Legion club. (unintelligible). I don't know if it was a birthday or anniversary, but they have a ballroom type place upstairs, and there was no way I was going to disassemble that…

78.t: Why Horace switched to the organ
78.s: Club owners would not pay for bass or a full band, so five men became three and Horace rented a Hammond organ and taught himself, about five or six years before 1975.
78.ch: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
78.q: : Well, let's see, Tom. I think the last five or six years. In fact, I wasn't too particular about it. It was more or less wished on me. It seemed to have been the trend, you know.

118.t: The folding piano and bad pianos
118.s: He was given a folding piano that was tuned at headquarters since local pianos were poor.
118.q: They gave me a piano to travel with. Oh. Yeah. And they're taking good care of the piano. And every time I returned back to headquarters they had a man to tune it.

667.s: Roy takes an electric piano because club pianos were bad, then tires of the cables and equipment and returns to acoustic.
667.ch: Rock era, electric piano, move east
667.q: It was fun, and we really enjoyed it for a couple of years, but then all of a sudden it got to be a big chore. Because we did not have somebody to come and set the stuff up.

746.t: Limits of the piano and attraction to electronics
746.s: She once wished to sustain and shape sound, sing, and use electronics, and hires others like Rothenberg and Teitelbaum for sound design.
746.q: Yeah. I used to feel that. I wanted to sing, I wanted other kinds of sounds, I wanted to be able to sustain and change a sound after I had played it which you can’t really do on a string instrument or a wind or a brass instrument, where vocally you can start soft and get louder. Well you can’t do…

754.t: The Fender Rhodes, fusion, and throwing the electric piano in the Hudson
754.s: Galper discusses the band's move to the Fender Rhodes and fusion, and explains why he dumped his electric piano in the Hudson River to commit to acoustic piano.
754.q: I couldn’t say anything. I don’t think I have an opinion about that. Because they were the first ones to use the Fender Rhodes. My piano was directly from Harry Rhodes’ factory. I think the move to the Fender Rhodes was the key to getting into the more fusion kind of thing. Yeah.

441.s: He has a Rhodes and a DX7, avoided synthesizers, and plans to take up the accordion again.
441.q: Not many. I have a Rhodes, I got into that, a wonderful Rhodes. I went to Europe for them for CBS Musical Instruments, and I bought one synthesizer which I have at home, a DX7, and that’s as far as I got.

755.s: Kirsh says Chick's Rhodes sound was already developed, from the Miles era.
755.q: No that was — I mean I recorded it — it depends which era you’re talking about. I mean he got into the Fender Rhodes early, before Bernie, but actually from Miles — Miles or shortly after Miles and liked it. I’m thinking originally he didn’t like it. I think he didn’t care for it and I think he…

159.t: Electric pianos, a Yamaha keyboard and notation software
159.s: He dislikes playing electric instruments, bought a keyboard for composing with the computer, and has Finale and Encore.
159.q: Not on a gig. I’m not fond of electric pianos or electronic instruments. To listen to them yes. To play them no. Because the touch is too different. Same with the organ. The organ is entirely different touch than playing the piano. But I like to listen to a lot of things. You know there’s a lot of…

344.s: Zawinul brought the tune to rehearsal in Teaneck; the band took up Wurlitzer and Rhodes.
344.q: Yeah. You know, we were always, well we were hoping, we were always experimenting. That band was experimenting all the time. And we played straight ahead jazz, we played all kinds of stuff. So when Joe brought that tune in, Zawinul, to, I think we were rehearsing in Teaneck, New Jersey. We…

345.t: Playing Fender Rhodes in a rock-jazz band on the Cape
345.s: McKenna played electric piano in Dick Johnson's band because the drummer was too loud, playing pop-rock tunes.
345.q: Oh, yeah, sure. I played the Fender Rhodes in a band. When I first went to the Cape we had a — Dick Johnson and Lou Columbo had like a six piece band and they wanted a little rock music, that the sort of rock jazz type guys can do. The drummer was so loud they had to get me a Fender Rhodes, or the…

756.t: Electronic keyboards, split keyboards and the mini Moog
756.s: Rowe watched his left hand at the Beeches. They discuss the electronic keyboard and the mini Moog Montalbano bought from Rowe.
756.ch: Working as a contractor and organist
756.q: Yes. It made things a lot easier to work. And of course, like you, I bought that mini Moog from you. I used to carry that thing around and put it on top of the Rhodes. It was always one keyboard or another. A little synthesizer you’d put on top, or sometimes it would be over to the left so I…

600.t: The Fender Rhodes: a 73 suitcase model, its mechanics and sound
600.s: Rydin liked the Rhodes sound but not its mechanics, added wheels, tuned it himself, and finally sold it for more than he paid.
600.q: Yes, in the 70s I did and in the 80s yes. In fact I liked it, I still like the sound of it but it has terrible mechanics. It’s not so nice to play on. But I do like the sound. But if I was Herbie Hancock and someone or other brought it for me — but it’s I mean, bringing this heavy to a gig and you…

757.s: The Wurlitzer predates the Rhodes, used by Ray Charles and Zawinul, giving keyboardists a volume control.
757.q: Yeah. Yeah. They had everything. And the Wurlitzer was before the Fender Rhodes. It was the first electric keyboard. You know that’s the one Ray Charles played on “What’d I Say” that just blew everybody’s mind.

512.t: The Fender Rhodes sound and Miles's pedals
512.s: He approached the Rhodes for its own colors rather than as a piano, and applied Miles's trumpet pedals to it.
512.q: Oh no. Oh it was right there. What happened was you know that’s why I got kind of upset because I think the Fender Rhodes did a documentary on the Fender Rhodes and I don’t know why they didn’t call. Because Chick and everyone else, and Herbie, they approached the Fender Rhodes the same way you…

164.t: Quitting studio work in 1972 to play only acoustic piano
164.s: Smith, free to pick his work, says that in 1972 he found he had worked a month without touching a piano because of synthesizers, and chose acoustic piano from then on.
164.q: Well it always has been from my standpoint. I’m one of the oddball musicians that went through the whole big band scene and everything, never smoked, never drank and hated drug addicts, so that was it.

618.s: He built a huge rig of Moog and other synths from about 1967 to 1978, left Columbia, and then returned to acoustic piano.

110.s: He used a Baldwin electric piano once on Gates of Justice; his sons use synthesizers.
110.q: So that’s the only time. But my sons have used synthesizers and electric keyboards.

143.t: Why he added an organ and why piano mattered
143.s: Piano rentals cost too much, so he bought an organ and pulled it in a U-Haul.
143.ch: Hiatus, Blues Walk and the road
143.q: Yes. Well, the reason I used an organ was because a lot of times we’d go into a place, and they didn’t have a piano—and renting a piano, that’s out of the question. People want a thousand dollars to rent a piano. Shit, a thousand dollars, we weren’t even making that much for the gig. So we decided…

509.s: She played about twenty organ gigs, with Walter Hamlet's organ, and some organ on the Ray Charles tribute.
509.q: Yeah. He‘s my daughter‘s godfather, and he‘s a very close friend of my family, and I used to go to all the joints, you know. He would play at some joints. I‘d go there and sit in with him, cut the foo [phonetic] and all. But maybe twenty gigs I played organ, when I wasn‘t just fooling around, you…

233.t: Clavinet and RMI keyboards: playing bass differently
233.s: In San Francisco he built a group of RMI, clavinet, drums and bass to avoid sounding like a traditional bassist.
233.q: : I was in San Francisco. I had taken an instrument up, a clavinnet. Clavinets were new on the scene. But I heard something there that I wanted to be involved with. It was electronic, and I guess I was getting into electronics, but getting into them...not freaking out in them. Because I could see…
